newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish government, trader welcome bourse alliance.
newsitem.headline: Danish government, trader welcome bourse alliance.

text.p: Danish Economy Minister Marianne Jelved on Thursday welcomed plans by the Danish and Swedish stock exchanges to launch a joint trading system, saying it would strengthen their competitiveness against other bourses.
"We see an increasing degree of internationalisation of financial markets and it is good that the Nordic markets are taking up the challenge," she said in a statement.
"The Nordic bourses are relatively small, taken individually, but combined they make up Europe's fifth-largest market in volume and can stand up to competition," she said.
"I hope that the other Nordic exchanges will take up the initiative."
The two founding partners said earlier that they saw their alliance as the first step toward a pan-Nordic securities market and had invited Finland, Iceland and Norway to join.
They expected the initial venture to boost the combined Stockholm and Copenhagen bourses' turnover by at least 10 percent.
Den Danske Bank chief dealer Michael Lindegaard agreed that the union would boost trade.
"The Danish market will get the most out of it because our companies will get substantially more attention and we expect that to bring more liquidity to the market," he said.
